definitions.explanation: Describes something that has just been ground, most commonly coffee beans, pepper, or flour.

examples.japanese: {挽|ひ}きたてのコーヒーは{香|かお}りがいい。
{挽|ひ}きたての{胡椒|こしょう}をかけた。
examples.english: I sprinkled freshly ground pepper on it.

examples.japanese: このカフェでは{毎朝|まいあさ}{挽|ひ}きたての{豆|まめ}でコーヒーを{淹|い}れている。
examples.english: This café brews coffee every morning using freshly ground beans.

notes:
A compound of {挽|ひ}く (to grind) and たて (just done, freshly). The たて suffix indicates something has just been completed and is at its freshest. Almost always used as a modifier with の: {挽|ひ}きたての〜. Most commonly associated with coffee, but also used for pepper, spices, and flour.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挽|ひ}きたてのコーヒー: freshly ground coffee
- {挽|ひ}きたての{豆|まめ}: freshly ground beans
- {挽|ひ}きたての{胡椒|こしょう}: freshly ground pepper

SIMILAR PATTERNS (〜たて):
- {焼|や}きたて: freshly baked
- {炊|た}きたて: freshly cooked (rice)
- {揚|あ}げたて: freshly fried
- {作|つく}りたて: freshly made
